record.paper_title: Whitehead's Asphericity Question and Its Relation to Other Open Problems
record.original_question: For a group ring such as QG, does the weak Bass trace conjecture hold, meaning that the Kaplansky trace and the augmentation trace agree on finitely generated projective modules over the group ring?

evidence.quote: equality of the Kaplansky and augmentation traces

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a discrete group and let $\mathbb{Q}G$ denote its rational group ring. For an idempotent matrix $A=(a_{ij})\in M_n(\mathbb{Q}G)$, define two traces of $A$:

1. The Kaplansky trace $\kappa(A)\in\mathbb{Q}$ is the sum $\sum_{i=1}^{n} c_e(a_{ii})$, where for $x=\sum_{g\in G} x_g\, g\in\mathbb{Q}G$ the coefficient $c_e(x)=x_e$ is the value at the identity element $e\in G$.

2. The augmentation trace $\varepsilon(A)\in\mathbb{Q}$ is $\sum_{i=1}^{n}\varepsilon(a_{ii})$, where $\varepsilon\colon\mathbb{Q}G\to\mathbb{Q}$ is the augmentation homomorphism sending $\sum_g x_g g$ to $\sum_g x_g$.

Both traces are invariant under conjugation by invertible matrices and additive under direct sums, so they descend to maps $K_0(\mathbb{Q}G)\to\mathbb{Q}$, denoted again by $\kappa$ and $\varepsilon$. Equivalently, for a finitely generated projective $\mathbb{Q}G$-module $P$ represented by an idempotent matrix $A$, one defines $\kappa(P):=\kappa(A)$ and $\varepsilon(P):=\varepsilon(A)$.

Weak Bass trace conjecture for $\mathbb{Q}G$: prove or disprove that for every finitely generated projective $\mathbb{Q}G$-module $P$,
$$\kappa(P)=\varepsilon(P).$$

Does this equality hold for every (discrete) group $G$?
artifact.category_tag: Bass trace conjecture for group rings
artifact.status_search_result: The weak Bass trace conjecture for QG is known to hold for large classes of groups (e.g. amenable groups, via Bost's conjecture, and groups satisfying the Farrell–Jones conjecture), but it remains open in general. Surveys and research papers continue to list it as an open problem and relate it to other conjectures such as Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture and the Farrell–Jones / Bost assembly conjectures.

status_evidence.title: From acyclic groups to the Bass conjecture for amenable groups
status_evidence.snippet: The Bost Conjecture on the ℓ¹-assembly map implies the Bass Conjecture; hence amenable groups satisfy the Bass Conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The weak Bass conjecture is known for amenable groups but remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Traces and the Bass conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Equality of the Kaplansky trace and augmentation trace on K_0(ZG) is the content of the (weak) Bass conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The formulation matches the weak Bass trace conjecture; it is the subject of ongoing research.

status_evidence.title: On the Farrell-Jones Conjecture and its applications
status_evidence.snippet: The Farrell-Jones Conjecture implies the Bass Conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The weak Bass conjecture follows from Farrell–Jones for many groups but remains open in full generality.
